brief.title: The Salt Ledger
brief.premise: In a city built on a tidal flat, a debt-clerk discovers that the tide-bound magic that keeps the sea out is being quietly overdrawn, and must expose the guild hiding the shortfall before the next spring tide.
constraints: Magic must always carry a visible physical cost.

world.name: Saltmere
world.description: Saltmere is a walled city on a tidal flat where tide-bound magic holds back the sea and every working of it is recorded as a debt in the Salt Clerks' ledgers.

locations.name: Ledger Hall
locations.description: The counting-house where tide-debts are recorded in salt-ink ledgers, built on the highest ground of the flat.

locations.name: Drowned Quay
locations.description: A harbour district that floods twice daily, home to ferrymen and smugglers.

locations.name: Brine Gate
locations.description: The great sluice-wall holding back the sea, protected by tide-bound wardings renewed each month.

locations.name: Mudflat Market
locations.description: A stilted bazaar on the exposed flats, open only at low tide.

factions.name: Salt Clerks
factions.description: A guild of accountants who record and ration tide-magic debts.

factions.name: Gate Wardens
factions.description: Warders who renew the wardings on the Brine Gate each month, paying for it with their own bodies.

factions.name: Quay Ferrymen
factions.description: Boatmen and smugglers who work the flooded streets and resent the clerks' levies.

rules.statement: Every working of tide-magic leaves a visible mark on the caster, such as salt-crusted skin or white hair.
Tide-bound wardings can be renewed only at the turn of a spring tide.
A tide-debt, once entered in the ledger, binds the debtor's family until it is paid.
Entries written in salt-ink cannot be altered without leaving a pale scar on the page.

history.name: The Founding of the Gate
history.description: Settlers raised the Brine Gate on the flat and bound it with the first tide-wardings.

history.name: The First Ledger
history.description: The Salt Clerks began recording tide-debts after the first warding renewal drained a ferryman's family of its savings.

history.name: The Great Flood
history.description: A warding lapsed and the sea flooded the Drowned Quay for a week, until the Gate Wardens renewed the wardings at the next spring tide.

history.name: The Market Charter
history.description: The Salt Clerks granted the Quay Ferrymen the right to trade on the flats at low tide in return for a levy.

conflicts.name: The Levy Dispute
conflicts.description: The Quay Ferrymen refuse to pay the Salt Clerks' rising levies on low-tide trade.

conflicts.name: The Overdrawn Gate
conflicts.description: The Gate Wardens suspect the Salt Clerks of hiding how much tide-magic the Brine Gate has already consumed.

characters.name: Ines Varro
characters.description: A junior debt-clerk at Ledger Hall who audits salt-ink entries and keeps a private tally of every correction she finds.
characters.motivation: To learn whether the Brine Gate's tide-debt is being hidden before the next spring tide.
characters.goal: Prove the shortfall in the ledgers and present it to the Gate Wardens.
characters.internal_conflict: She owes her post to the guild she is about to expose.
characters.external_conflict: Senior clerks bury her audit requests.

abilities.name: Salt-ink reading
abilities.description: Spots erased or recopied entries by the pale scars and fresh ink they leave on the page.

characters.arc: Ines learns that records are only as honest as the people who keep them.

characters.name: Oren Dask
characters.description: The ledger-master of Ledger Hall, who hides the Brine Gate's shortfall by recopying whole ledger pages instead of correcting them.
characters.motivation: To keep the guild's credit intact until the next spring tide.
characters.goal: Silence Ines and keep the shortfall off the record.
characters.internal_conflict: He knows the gate cannot be renewed on the guild's accounts alone.
characters.external_conflict: The Gate Wardens demand a full audit.

abilities.name: Page-recopying
abilities.description: Recopies a ledger page in a close imitation of the original hand, so that only the fresh ink gives it away.

characters.arc: Oren's concealment collapses when the Wardens demand the original pages.

characters.name: Tamsin Reel
characters.description: A ferrywoman whose family is bound by a tide-debt entered before she was born.
characters.motivation: To free her family from a debt it never chose.
characters.goal: Find the ledger entry that created the debt and have it cancelled.
characters.internal_conflict: She resents the clerks but needs Ines's access.
characters.external_conflict: The clerks levy her low-tide trade.

abilities.name: Flood-navigation
abilities.description: Poles a ferry through the Drowned Quay's streets at any tide.

characters.arc: Tamsin learns the debt can be challenged openly rather than dodged.

relationships.description: Oren trained Ines and still reviews her audits.
Tamsin gives Ines access to the quay's unofficial tide records in return for help tracing her family's debt.
Oren's office holds the entry that binds Tamsin's family.

storyboard.title: The Salt Ledger
storyboard.logline: Ines uncovers the hidden shortfall in the Brine Gate's tide-debt and must expose it before the next spring tide.

scenes.title: The Gate Ledger
scenes.summary: Ines audits the Brine Gate's tide-debt entries at Ledger Hall.
scenes.goal: Audit the Brine Gate's tide-debt entries.
scenes.outcome: She finds ledger pages for the Brine Gate written in fresh ink.

scenes.title: The Quay Records
scenes.summary: Tamsin shows Ines the quay's unofficial tide records and the debt that binds her family, and says the quay remembers a time before the ledgers, though no record survives.
scenes.goal: Trade the tide records for help tracing the debt.
scenes.outcome: Ines gets the records and promises to trace the debt.

scenes.title: The Gap
scenes.summary: Ines compares the quay's tide records with the gate ledger and finds that the Brine Gate has consumed far more tide-magic than the ledger shows.
scenes.conflict: Oren checks her work and grows suspicious.
scenes.outcome: Ines has proof of a shortfall, and Oren knows she has it.

scenes.title: The Audit Closed
scenes.summary: Oren confronts Ines at Ledger Hall and orders the audit closed, warning that he can recopy any page he likes.
scenes.goal: Silence Ines and close the audit.
scenes.conflict: She refuses to hand over her notes.
scenes.outcome: Ines smuggles her notes out to Tamsin at the quay.

scenes.title: The Wardens
scenes.summary: Ines takes her notes from Tamsin to the Gate Wardens at the Brine Gate and shows them the gap between the records.
scenes.conflict: The Wardens fear another failed renewal.
scenes.outcome: The Wardens agree to demand the original ledger pages at the spring-tide renewal.

scenes.title: The Original Pages
scenes.summary: On the day of the spring-tide renewal the Wardens demand the original pages; Ines proves the pages were recopied by their fresh ink, and Oren's concealment collapses.
scenes.goal: Expose the recopied pages before the wardings are renewed.
scenes.conflict: Oren tries to destroy the original pages before the Wardens can read them.
scenes.outcome: The original pages are produced and the true shortfall is entered in the ledger.

scenes.title: The Renewal
scenes.summary: That evening the Gate Wardens renew the wardings at the turn of the spring tide, paying the cost with their own bodies, on the corrected accounts.
scenes.goal: Renew the gate on honest accounts.
scenes.conflict: Renewal costs the Wardens visible marks, and the Clerks resist the corrected levy.
scenes.outcome: The gate holds, and Tamsin's family debt is reopened for open challenge.

evidence_quotes: says the quay remembers a time before the ledgers, though no record survives

evidence_summary: Tamsin's remark about a time before the ledgers is unverified quay memory, not a contradiction of the history.
